title: John Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on John chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: John Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of John Chapter 15.

questions.question: In John 15, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch
If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will
As the Father hath loved me, so have I loved you
questions.explanation: John 15:1 is the opening statement in the chapter, declaring 'I am the true vine'.

questions.question: Who is described as the husbandman in John 15?
questions.explanation: John 15:1 states 'I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.'

questions.question: What happens to every branch in Jesus that does not bear fruit?
questions.explanation: John 15:2 says 'Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away.'

questions.question: According to John 15, how are the branches that do bear fruit treated?
options: They are purged so they may bring forth more fruit
questions.correctAnswer: They are purged so they may bring forth more fruit
questions.explanation: John 15:2 states 'and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.'

questions.question: How are the disciples described as being made clean?
options: Through the word Jesus has spoken unto them
questions.correctAnswer: Through the word Jesus has spoken unto them
questions.explanation: John 15:3 states 'Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.'

questions.question: What must happen for a branch to bear fruit, according to John 15?
options: It must abide in the vine
It must grow on a strong tree
questions.correctAnswer: It must abide in the vine
questions.explanation: John 15:4 states 'As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine.'

questions.question: Who is the vine and who are the branches in John 15?
options: Jesus is the vine, and the disciples are the branches
The Father is the vine, and Jesus is the branches
The disciples are the vine, and Jesus is the branches
The vine is a tree, and Jesus is the gardener
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is the vine, and the disciples are the branches
questions.explanation: John 15:5 says 'I am the vine, ye are the branches.'

questions.question: What happens to a man who does not abide in Jesus, according to John 15?
options: He is cast forth as a branch and withered
He is pruned to bear more fruit
questions.correctAnswer: He is cast forth as a branch and withered
questions.explanation: John 15:6 states 'If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered.'

questions.question: What will happen if you abide in Jesus and His words abide in you?
options: You shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you
You will be free from sin
questions.correctAnswer: You shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you
questions.explanation: John 15:7 says 'If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you.'

questions.question: How is the Father glorified according to John 15?
questions.explanation: John 15:8 states 'Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit.'

questions.question: How does Jesus say He has loved the disciples?
options: As the Father hath loved Him
questions.correctAnswer: As the Father hath loved Him
questions.explanation: John 15:9 says 'As the Father hath loved me, so have I loved you.'

questions.question: True or False: Jesus says that without Him you can do nothing.
questions.explanation: John 15:5 states 'for without me ye can do nothing.'

questions.question: True or False: Jesus commands the disciples to continue in His love.
questions.explanation: John 15:9 says 'continue ye in my love.'

questions.question: True or False: John 15 says branches that do not bear fruit are watered more.
questions.explanation: John 15:2 says branches that do not bear fruit are taken away, not watered more.

questions.question: True or False: The passage states that the Father is the vine and Jesus is the husbandman.
questions.explanation: John 15:1 clearly states Jesus is the true vine and the Father is the husbandman.

medium.title: John Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from John Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What command does Jesus give in John 15:12?
options: That ye love one another, as I have loved you
questions.correctAnswer: That ye love one another, as I have loved you
questions.explanation: This is found in John 15:12, where Jesus explicitly states this commandment to His disciples.

questions.question: What does John 15:11 promise will happen if someone keeps Jesus' commandments as stated in John 15:10?
questions.explanation: John 15:11 says that Jesus spoke these things so His joy might remain in them and their joy might be full, which is a direct result of keeping His commandments.

questions.question: According to John 15:13, what is the greatest form of love?
options: To lay down one's life for friends
questions.correctAnswer: To lay down one's life for friends
questions.explanation: This is stated in John 15:13, emphasizing the sacrificial nature of true love.

questions.question: What does John 15:15 reveal about the relationship between Jesus and His followers?
questions.explanation: In John 15:15, Jesus mentions that He calls them friends, indicating a close relationship based on shared knowledge and purpose.

questions.question: What is the fruit that Jesus refers to in John 15:16?
questions.explanation: John 15:16 indicates that He chose His disciples to go and bring forth fruit, which refers to the spiritual results of their ministry.

questions.question: In John 15:17, what does Jesus command His followers to do?
questions.explanation: John 15:17 reiterates the command to love one another, emphasizing its importance in the community of believers.

questions.question: What does John 15:18 say about the relationship between the world and Jesus' followers?
questions.explanation: In John 15:18, Jesus warns that if the world hates His followers, it is because it hated Him first, indicating the opposition they will face.

questions.question: How does abiding in Jesus relate to bearing fruit as mentioned in John 15:5?
options: Without abiding, one can still bear fruit
Abiding in Him is essential for bearing much fruit
Abiding is not necessary for disciples
Bearing fruit is independent of relationship
questions.correctAnswer: Abiding in Him is essential for bearing much fruit
questions.explanation: John 15:5 states that without abiding in Jesus, one can do nothing, highlighting the necessity of this relationship for spiritual productivity.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you' in John 15:16?
options: It emphasizes divine selection and purpose
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes divine selection and purpose
questions.explanation: John 15:16 makes clear that Jesus chooses His followers for a specific purpose, which is to bear fruit.

questions.question: What does John 15:3 say about the effect of Jesus' words on His followers?
questions.explanation: John 15:3 states that the disciples are clean through the word Jesus has spoken, indicating the purifying power of His teachings.

questions.question: According to John 15:2, what happens to branches that do not bear fruit?
questions.explanation: John 15:2 specifies that every branch in Him that does not bear fruit is taken away, illustrating the seriousness of spiritual fruitlessness.

questions.question: What is the relationship between love and obedience as suggested in John 15:10?
options: Obedience is a result of love
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience is a result of love
questions.explanation: John 15:10 indicates that keeping Jesus' commandments is how one abides in His love, establishing a clear connection between love and obedience.

questions.question: In the context of John 15:4, to what does 'abide in me' refer?
questions.explanation: Abiding in Jesus refers to maintaining a close relationship with Him, as emphasized in John 15:4.

questions.question: Is it true that bearing much fruit glorifies the Father according to John 15:8?
questions.explanation: John 15:8 states that bearing much fruit glorifies the Father, affirming the importance of spiritual productivity.

questions.question: Does John 15:6 suggest that those who do not abide in Jesus will be fruitful?
questions.explanation: John 15:6 clearly indicates that if a man does not abide in Jesus, he is cast forth and cannot bear fruit.

hard.title: John Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from John Chapter 15.

questions.question: What does Jesus say about the world in relation to His followers?
questions.explanation: This is stated in John 15:19, where Jesus explains that because He has chosen them out of the world, the world hates them.

questions.question: What does Jesus say will happen to His followers if they are persecuted?
questions.explanation: John 15:20 states that if they have persecuted Jesus, they will also persecute His followers.

questions.question: Why will the world do these things to Jesus' followers?
options: Because they are His chosen ones
Because they know not Him that sent Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: Because they know not Him that sent Jesus
questions.explanation: According to John 15:21, all these things will be done for Jesus' name's sake because they do not know the one who sent Him.

questions.question: What does Jesus imply about the guilt of those who heard His words?
questions.explanation: John 15:22 indicates that because Jesus came and spoke to them, they now have no cloke for their sin.

questions.question: What is the relationship between hating Jesus and hating the Father?
options: Hating Jesus means loving the Father
He that hateth me hateth my Father also
Only the Father is to be loved
questions.correctAnswer: He that hateth me hateth my Father also
questions.explanation: This is clearly stated in John 15:23, which connects the hatred of Jesus with the hatred of the Father.

questions.question: What fulfills the prophecy mentioned in John 15:25?
options: They loved me without a cause
They hated me without a cause
They admired me without a cause
They ignored me without a cause
questions.correctAnswer: They hated me without a cause
questions.explanation: John 15:25 references the fulfillment of the law that states they hated Jesus without a cause.

questions.question: What does the term 'Comforter' refer to in John 15:26?
questions.explanation: In John 15:26, the Comforter refers to the Spirit of truth that Jesus will send from the Father.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'martureo' in John 15:27 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'martureo' means to witness, as indicated in John 15:27 where the disciples will bear witness.

questions.question: What literary device is used in John 15:12 where Jesus commands love?
questions.explanation: The command to love one another in John 15:12 is framed by Jesus' statements on love, forming an inclusio.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects with the theme of being chosen as in John 15:19?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 2:9 echoes the theme of being chosen as a royal priesthood, similar to John 15:19.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects with the theme of bearing fruit as in John 15:8?
questions.explanation: Galatians 5:22-23 discusses the fruits of the Spirit, complementing the theme of bearing fruit in John 15:8.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Jesus' statement in John 15:19?
options: He tells them to love one another
questions.explanation: The verse immediately before John 15:19 discusses the world's hatred towards His followers, setting the context for His warning.

questions.question: What comes immediately after Jesus' statement in John 15:20?
questions.explanation: Immediately after John 15:20, Jesus speaks about those who do not know the Father, continuing the theme of their rejection.

questions.question: The world is said to love its own. Is this statement True?
questions.explanation: This is true as stated in John 15:19, where it is affirmed that the world loves its own.

questions.question: Jesus claims that the servant is greater than his lord. Is this statement True?
questions.explanation: This is false; Jesus states that the servant is not greater than his lord in John 15:20.

theological.title: John Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from John Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does John 15:2 teach about sanctification?
options: God purges fruitful branches so they may bear more fruit
God removes all branches regardless of fruitfulness
Fruitfulness is irrelevant to the believer's standing
Branches are perfected by their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: God purges fruitful branches so they may bear more fruit
questions.explanation: John 15:2 explains that every branch bearing fruit is purged by the Father to bring forth more fruit, showing God's active role in sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine does John 15:7 teach about prayer and divine promise?
options: Abiding in Christ and His words ensures prayers will be answered
Prayer is only effective when offered in solitude
God answers prayers only when they align with human desires
Prayer is a test of faith but not guaranteed to be answered
questions.correctAnswer: Abiding in Christ and His words ensures prayers will be answered
questions.explanation: John 15:7 teaches that if believers abide in Christ and His words abide in them, their prayers will be granted, emphasizing the connection between abiding and answered prayer.

questions.question: What doctrine does John 15:13 teach about the nature of love?
options: The greatest love is laying down one’s life for friends
Love is primarily an emotional feeling without action
Love is measured by reciprocal benefits
Love is proven only through verbal affirmation
questions.correctAnswer: The greatest love is laying down one’s life for friends
questions.explanation: John 15:13 defines the highest form of love as sacrificially laying down one’s life for friends, teaching the doctrine of self-giving love.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does John 15:9 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: John 15:9 shows Jesus commanding believers to continue in His love as the Father loved Him, demonstrating God's unconditional love.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does John 15:26 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: John 15:26 reveals God's faithfulness in sending the Comforter (Spirit of truth) from the Father to testify of Christ.

questions.question: How does John 15:14 connect to the broader biblical theme of discipleship?
options: It defines friendship with Christ through obedience to His commands
It emphasizes works as the sole requirement for salvation
It prioritizes ritual observance over personal relationship
It teaches isolation from the world as the mark of discipleship
questions.correctAnswer: It defines friendship with Christ through obedience to His commands
questions.explanation: John 15:14 links discipleship with friendship to Christ, conditioned on obedience, echoing themes of covenant faithfulness in Scripture.

questions.question: How does John 15:18 connect to redemptive history in relation to the world’s hostility?
options: It shows believers will face the same hatred Christ did from the world
It promises the world will ultimately accept believers
It teaches that believers are exempt from persecution
It states that hatred is a sign of divine judgment on believers
questions.correctAnswer: It shows believers will face the same hatred Christ did from the world
questions.explanation: John 15:18 teaches that the world hated Christ first and will hate His followers similarly, connecting to the theme of persecution of God’s people throughout redemptive history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses John 15:4 and John 15:5 teach about the believer's union with Christ?
options: Abiding in Christ is essential for spiritual fruitfulness and dependence
Believers can bear fruit independently of Christ
Union with Christ is symbolic, not vital for sanctification
Fruitfulness depends mainly on human effort
questions.correctAnswer: Abiding in Christ is essential for spiritual fruitfulness and dependence
questions.explanation: John 15:4 and 15:5 emphasize that branches (believers) cannot bear fruit unless they abide in the vine (Christ), teaching vital union and dependence on Him.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 15:22 and John 15:24 teach about human accountability and sin?
options: The works and words of Christ expose sin and remove any excuse
Sin remains hidden if Christ’s works are ignored
Sin is not charged if one rejects Christ’s works
Accountability is based solely on the Law, not Christ’s ministry
questions.correctAnswer: The works and words of Christ expose sin and remove any excuse
questions.explanation: John 15:22 and 15:24 state that without Christ’s coming and works, people would not have sin; now they have no cloak for their sin, teaching full accountability.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 15:16 and John 15:8 teach about Christian fruitfulness and election?
options: Believers are chosen by Christ to bear lasting fruit that glorifies the Father
Fruitfulness is unrelated to election or divine purpose
Fruitfulness is a human achievement independent of divine choice
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are chosen by Christ to bear lasting fruit that glorifies the Father
questions.explanation: John 15:16 and 15:8 teach that Christ chose believers to bring forth fruit that glorifies God, linking election with obedient discipleship and fruitfulness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim John 15:6 teaches that all who do not bear fruit are eternally condemned without hope. What does John 15:6 actually teach?
options: Branches not abiding in Christ are cast out, withered, and burned, illustrating judgment
All non-fruitful branches will eventually bear fruit without judgment
God arbitrarily condemns believers regardless of fruitfulness
The verse only refers to temporary discipline with no final consequence
questions.correctAnswer: Branches not abiding in Christ are cast out, withered, and burned, illustrating judgment
questions.explanation: John 15:6 depicts branches not abiding in Christ as withered and cast into the fire, symbolizing judgment due to separation from Christ.

questions.question: What doctrine does John 15:17 teach about the nature of Christian community?
options: The command to love one another is foundational to Christian life
Community is optional and secondary to individual piety
Love is only to be shown to those outside the church
Obedience to laws supersedes love in community
questions.correctAnswer: The command to love one another is foundational to Christian life
questions.explanation: John 15:17 commands believers to love one another, establishing love as the core ethic of Christian community.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does John 15:10 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: John 15:10 relates abiding in love to keeping commandments, showing Jesus’ obedience to the Father and God’s covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: How does John 15:20 prepare for the theme of persecution in the New Testament church?
options: It warns believers that persecution of Christ predicts persecution of His followers
It promises no persecution will come to believers
It teaches that persecution is a sign of God’s rejection
It encourages believers to avoid suffering by hiding their faith
questions.correctAnswer: It warns believers that persecution of Christ predicts persecution of His followers
questions.explanation: John 15:20 teaches that since Christ was persecuted, His followers will also be persecuted, preparing the church for trials.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 15:3 and John 15:11 teach about the role of Christ's word in sanctification and joy?
options: Christ’s word cleanses believers and sustains their full joy
Joy comes independently of Christ’s word
Sanctification is unrelated to hearing Christ’s teaching
Believers are justified by works, not by Christ’s word
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s word cleanses believers and sustains their full joy
questions.explanation: John 15:3 states believers are clean through Christ’s word, and 15:11 links Christ’s words to full joy, teaching sanctification and joy through His word.
